claims.paraphrase: Page title.
The Library screen, named Library in the sidebar, lists the site images without a draft open.
An account can lack the Library sidebar entry.
Section heading.
The library shows counts, used total, and storage, a name and alt search, and a grid or list view toggle.
Three filters: All, Needs alt, and No references found.
No references found is not proof an image is unused.
Section heading.
The detail panel shows a large preview, name, address, and where-used entries linking to their editors.
The Default alt text field seeds new placements and leaves existing placements untouched.
Save on the detail panel commits the edits.
Section heading.
JPEG, PNG, WebP, and GIF are accepted directly and HEIC is converted automatically.
Many phones save photos as HEIC.
Section heading.
Replace image uploads a new file and reviews the published entries that will repoint plus open edits that keep the old file.
Replacing needs the address typed every time and names how many entries change.
Section heading.
Push alt to placements fills placements lacking alt from the default, only overwrites custom alt on request, and previews the changes.
Push alt fills gaps only and leaves per-placement alt unless overwrite is chosen.
Section heading.
An unused image gets a plain confirmation; a used one lists what breaks and needs its address typed; git keeps every version.
Section heading.
A selection checkbox sits at the top-left of a grid tile or in the first list column.
Grid view supports Space, Shift+Arrow, and Ctrl or Cmd+A for selection.
Selecting opens a bar with the count, Select all, and Delete.
A bulk delete shows first which selected images are still in use.
A bulk delete skips and names anything still in use rather than deleting it.
Section heading.
Find orphaned files scans for stored files absent from the library; deleting needs the count typed and cannot be undone.
Advice that the orphan scan is housekeeping and to ask the owner if unsure.
Continuation of the advice to ask the owner first.
Horizontal rule.
A freshness stamp naming a review date.
